## R-323 · Op-amp compensation, gain boosting, CMFB and loop-gain literature (Course 20)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent. IEEE Xplore refused automated access; IEEE abstracts were read through the Crossref and OpenAlex APIs (publisher abstracts) and, where available, author or university repository copies.*

- **Indirect compensation:** B. K. Ahuja, "An improved frequency compensation technique for CMOS operational amplifiers," *IEEE JSSC* SC-18(6), pp. 629–633, Dec. 1983, DOI 10.1109/JSSC.1983.1052012. Abstract: the RC-compensated two-stage op-amp has a limited capacitive-load range and its supply rejection "shows severe degradation above the open-loop pole frequency"; the new technique gives a much wider load range and better negative-supply rejection; measured 70 dB negative-supply rejection at 100 kHz and 58 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz (n-well CMOS). The abstract does not describe the circuit; the cascode/current-buffer description is the later literature's.
- **PSRR of Miller OTAs:** M. S. J. Steyaert and W. M. C. Sansen, "Power supply rejection ratio in operational transconductance amplifiers," *IEEE Trans. Circuits Syst.* 37(9), pp. 1077–1084, Sep. 1990, DOI 10.1109/31.57596: the single-stage OTA's PSRR is "one order of magnitude better than the commonly used Miller OTA". Supporting: TI SLOA011B (Karki), §5.11: datasheet PSRR is a DC parameter that "falls off as the frequency increases".
- **Gain boosting:** K. Bult and G. J. G. M. Geelen, "A fast-settling CMOS op amp for SC circuits with 90-dB DC gain," *IEEE JSSC* 25(6), pp. 1379–1384, 1990, DOI 10.1109/4.62165. Abstract: 1.6 µm CMOS; 90 dB DC gain and 116 MHz unity-gain frequency into 16 pF; single-pole settling at feedback factor 1/3 with 18 MHz closed-loop bandwidth into 35 pF and better than 0.03 % accuracy; 5 V supply, about 4.2 V swing; boosting costs 30 % area and 15 % power. Absolute power and settling time in ns are not in the abstract.
- **Nested Miller:** R. G. H. Eschauzier, L. P. T. Kerklaan and J. H. Huijsing, "A 100-MHz 100-dB operational amplifier with multipath nested Miller compensation structure," *IEEE JSSC* 27(12), pp. 1709–1717, Dec. 1992, DOI 10.1109/4.173096 (read from the TU Delft repository copy). A **bipolar** (all-npn) design: 100 dB, 100 MHz unity-gain bandwidth, 40° phase margin into 100 pF, 0.1 % settling in 60 ns for a 1 V step; plain NMC 60 MHz and 70 ns. Its eqs. (1)–(3) state the Butterworth design rule (stages numbered from the output); relabelled input-first it is C_m1 = 4g_m1C_L/g_m3, C_m2 = 2g_m2C_L/g_m3. Review: K. N. Leung and P. K. T. Mok, "Analysis of multistage amplifier-frequency compensation," *IEEE TCAS-I* 48(9), pp. 1041–1056, Sep. 2001, DOI 10.1109/81.948432 (metadata confirmed; equations not read).
- **Ring amplifiers:** B. Hershberg et al., "Ring amplifiers for switched capacitor circuits," *IEEE JSSC* 47(12), pp. 2928–2942, Dec. 2012, DOI 10.1109/JSSC.2012.2217865: a 15-bit pipelined ADC in 0.18 µm CMOS with 76.8 dB SNDR and 95.4 dB SFDR at 20 MS/s, 5.1 mW, 45 fJ/conversion-step; a 10.5-bit ring-amplifier-only ADC at 61.5 dB SNDR. ISSCC 2012 version DOI 10.1109/ISSCC.2012.6177090.
- **Switched-capacitor CMFB:** D. Senderowicz et al., "A family of differential NMOS analog circuits for a PCM codec filter chip," *IEEE JSSC* SC-17(6), pp. 1014–1023, Dec. 1982 (abstract does not mention CMFB); US Patent 4,574,250 (Senderowicz, Intel; filed 13 Oct 1981): a switched-capacitor sampler that "serves as a common mode feedback"; R. Castello and P. R. Gray, "A high-performance micropower switched-capacitor filter," *IEEE JSSC* SC-20(6), pp. 1122–1132, Dec. 1985, whose abstract names "switched-capacitor common-mode feedback".
- **Loop-gain measurement:** R. D. Middlebrook, "Measurement of loop gain in feedback systems," *Int. J. Electronics* 38(4), pp. 485–512, Apr. 1975, DOI 10.1080/00207217508920421 (voltage and current injection without opening the loop, combined when neither alone suffices); M. Tian, V. Visvanathan, J. Hantgan and K. Kundert, "Striving for small-signal stability," *IEEE Circuits and Devices Magazine* 17(1), pp. 31–41, Jan. 2001, DOI 10.1109/101.900125 (a two-port loop method including reverse transmission, plus device-based gain nulling). NOT CONFIRMED and not used: the closed-form double-injection combination formula; which commercial simulators implement Tian's method.

## R-324 · Published figures of merit of multistage CMOS OTAs (Course 20)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent from the open-access accepted version of Grasso et al. (TCAS-II 2018), Table IV, and from the cited papers' abstracts (OpenAlex).*

- Many papers define FOM_S = GBW·C_L/Power (MHz·pF/mW) and FOM_L = SR·C_L/Power; current-normalized versions are often called IFOM_S/IFOM_L. The course computes $f_uC_L/I$ (MHz·pF/mA) from each paper's reported GBW, load and current.
- From Grasso, Marano, Palumbo and Pennisi, "High-performance three-stage single-Miller CMOS OTA with no upper limit of C_L," *IEEE TCAS-II* 65(11), pp. 1529–1533, Nov. 2018, DOI 10.1109/TCSII.2017.2756923, Table IV (GBW, C_L, current): Tan & Ki (JSSC Feb 2015) 3.37 MHz, 680 pF, 10.5 µA; Marano et al. (TCAS-I Sep 2016) 2.72 MHz, 10 nF, 24.49 µA; Qu et al. (JSSC Feb 2017) 1.18 MHz, 18 nF, 58 µA; Grasso et al. 0.91 MHz at 30 nF, 1.70 MHz at 10 nF, 0.43 MHz at 100 nF, 6.36 µA. Qin et al., "Dual AC boosting compensation scheme for multistage amplifiers," *IEEE TCAS-II* 64(8), pp. 882–886, Aug. 2017 (abstract): 0.52 MHz into 3200 pF, 60 µW from ±0.8 V (37.5 µA).
- Computed $f_uC_L/I$: 4.4 × 10⁴ (Qin) to 6.8 × 10⁶ MHz·pF/mA (Grasso, 100 nF). Caveats: Tan & Ki's own abstract gives 560 pF and 3.49 MHz, not the table's 680 pF and 3.37 MHz; Marano's reported FOMs differ by about 2 % from the table's own inputs.

## R-326 · Bandgap reference literature, recent CMOS references, ngspice BJT temperature parameters (Course 20)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent. ieeexplore.ieee.org and analog.com were unreachable; IEEE abstracts were read through Crossref and OpenAlex, Tsividis (1980) from a publicly posted copy (page images), and ngspice from the official SourceForge files.*

- **Foundations:** R. J. Widlar, "New developments in IC voltage regulators," *IEEE JSSC* SC-6(1), pp. 2–7, Feb. 1971 (a temperature-compensated reference "with numerous advantages over zener diodes"); K. E. Kuijk, "A precision reference voltage source," *IEEE JSSC* SC-8(3), pp. 222–226, June 1973 (output temperature-independent when the sum "equals the gap voltage of silicon"; a 10 V reference, −250 µV over ±10 K, 10 ppm/month); A. P. Brokaw, "A simple three-terminal IC bandgap reference," *IEEE JSSC* SC-9(6), pp. 388–393, Dec. 1974 (collector-current sensing, 2.5 V, 5 ppm/°C over "the military temperature range").
- **Tsividis 1980:** "Accurate analysis of temperature effects in I_C–V_BE characteristics with application to bandgap reference sources," *IEEE JSSC* SC-15(6), pp. 1076–1084, Dec. 1980, DOI 10.1109/JSSC.1980.1051519. Eq. (12) gives V_BE(T) with the nonlinear gap V_G(T) and η ≡ 4 − n; the extrapolated V_G0r = 1.20595 V (T_r ≥ 300 K); fitted η for five processes 2.330, 2.303, 2.286, 2.316, 2.405; fitting the linear-bandgap form (eq. 38) instead needs "fictitious" η = 3.429 and V_G0 = 1.1761 V (process V). Eq. (14): the zero-TC output is V_G0r + (η − θ_r)kT_r/q (θ_r = 1 for PTAT bias); the course evaluates it as 1.239–1.242 V at 300 K.
- **Sub-1 V:** H. Banba et al., "A CMOS bandgap reference circuit with sub-1-V operation," *IEEE JSSC* 34(5), pp. 670–674, May 1999, DOI 10.1109/4.760378: 0.4 µm flash process; conventional V_ref "about 1.25 V"; measured 518 ± 15 mV (3σ), 23 samples, 27–125 °C (the 1998 VLSI version says 515 mV). Minimum supply, TC and current NOT CONFIRMED (not in the abstract).
- **Recent CMOS references (abstracts):** G. Ge, C. Zhang, G. Hoogzaad, K. A. A. Makinwa, *IEEE JSSC* 46(11), pp. 2693–2701, Nov. 2011: ±0.15 % (3σ), −40 to 125 °C, single trim; residual error "mainly PTAT, and can be removed by a single room temperature trim"; 55 µA from 1.8 V, 0.16 µm. I. Lee, D. Sylvester, D. Blaauw, *IEEE JSSC* 52(5), pp. 1443–1449, May 2017: 35 pW from 1.4 V, ±1.0 % (3σ) 0–100 °C after one trim, 0.18 µm. Y. Ji et al., *IEEE JSSC* 54(12), pp. 3281–3291, Dec. 2019: 192 pW; untrimmed 0.53 %, 0.020 %/V and 33 ppm/°C over 45 chips. U. Kamath et al., *IEEE JSSC* 54(7), pp. 1830–1840, July 2019: 1 V bandgap in 7 nm FinFET, ±0.2 % and 6 ppm/°C from −45 to 125 °C. J.-H. Boo et al., *IEEE JSSC* 56(4), pp. 1197–1206, Apr. 2021: +0.02 %/−0.12 % (3σ), −40 to 125 °C, single trim, 17 µA from 1.8 V. K. Chen et al., *IEEE JSSC* 56(1), pp. 267–276, Jan. 2021: 1.16 V, ±8.2 mV across seven untrimmed samples (±0.71 %).
- **ngspice:** User's Manual v47 (Aug. 2026), §7.3.3: Gummel–Poon EG default 1.11 eV, XTI default 3, TNOM 27 °C; source bjttemp.c: IS(T) = IS (T/T_nom)^XTI exp[qEG(T − T_nom)/(kT T_nom)], the linear-bandgap form with EG as V_g0 and XTI as η.

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent. ieeexplore.ieee.org was not used; IEEE abstracts were read through OpenAlex and cross-checked against Crossref for volume, issue, pages and author spellings. Numbers are as stated in the abstracts.*

- **Rincón-Mora & Allen**, "A low-voltage, low quiescent current, low drop-out regulator," *IEEE JSSC* 33(1), pp. 36–44, Jan. 1998, DOI 10.1109/4.654935: operates down to 1 V input; 23 µA zero-load quiescent current; 18 mA at 1 V and 50 mA at 1.2 V input; exploits the load dependence of the frequency response to minimize quiescent current. - **Hazucha et al.**, "Area-efficient linear regulator with ultra-fast load regulation," *IEEE JSSC* 40(4), pp. 933–940, Apr. 2005, DOI 10.1109/JSSC.2004.842831 (VLSI Symp. 2004 version, DOI 10.1109/VLSIC.2004.1346565): 90 nm; 1.2 V in, 0.9 V out; 0.54 ns response time at 94 % current efficiency; 90 mV peak-to-peak droop for a 100 mA step with 0.6 nF on-chip; 0.2 V minimum dropout at 100 mA; regulator 0.008 mm², capacitor 0.090 mm². Response time T_R = CΔV/ΔI (definition attributed to this paper by L. He et al., *Sensors* 22(23), 9367, 2022, DOI 10.3390/s22239367; 0.6 nF × 90 mV/100 mA = 0.54 ns matches exactly). Medium confidence for the definition. **UNVERIFIED:** the origin of the quiescent-current-weighted FoM T_R·I_Q/ΔI; FoM conventions differ between papers, so published FoMs are not recomputed here.

IEEE CICC*, Sep. 2010, DOI 10.1109/CICC.2010.5617586: 0.5 V in, 0.45 V out; 98.7 % current efficiency and 2.7 µA quiescent current at 200 µA load; op-amp LDOs "fail to operate at 0.5V". ## R-332 · Sampling jitter: formula, surveys and published values (Course 20)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent from TI documents (ti.com), OpenAlex/Crossref abstracts and the Murmann survey files (raw.githubusercontent.com).*

- **Formula:** T. Neu, "Clock jitter analyzed in the time domain, Part 1," TI *Analog Applications Journal* SLYT379, 3Q 2010: "SNR_Jitter[dBc] = −20 × log(2π × f_IN × t_Jitter)"; total jitter is the root-sum-square of clock-input and ADC aperture jitter; aperture jitter rises as the clock slew rate falls; example 400 fs at 100 MHz → 72 dBc. Re-read 24 Nov 2026 (pp. 5–9): "A 14-bit pipeline converter typically has a thermal noise of ~70 to 74 dB"; "A 16-bit ADC, for example, has a thermal noise floor of ~77 to 80 dB" (the 16-bit sentence does not say pipeline); 73 dB thermal plus 400 fs at 100 MHz gives 69.5 dBc. Part 2 (SLYT389, 4Q 2010) gives measured baselines instead: ADS54RF63 64.4 dBFS, ADS5483 79.1 dBFS. National Semiconductor AN-775 (TI SNOA223), 1992: aperture jitter specified as rms; peak-slope rule f_max = 1/(2π t_aj 2^n).
- **Walden:** R. H. Walden, *IEEE JSAC* 17(4), pp. 539–550, Apr. 1999, DOI 10.1109/49.761034: from about 2 MS/s to 4 GS/s resolution falls about 1 bit per doubling of sample rate, attributed to aperture jitter; comparator ambiguity limits multi-GS/s rates. Body text UNVERIFIED.
- **Murmann survey:** "ADC Performance Survey 1997-2026," github.com/bmurmann/ADC-survey, latest revision 20260801 (VLSI 2026 update); jitter lines for 1 ps and 0.1 ps (64.04 dB at 1 GHz for 0.1 ps). ISSCC 2022 short course: "High-speed ADCs and DACs: Tens of femtoseconds timing jitter"; τ ≈ 3 ps "in leading-edge technology". Implied jitter bounds of about 51–55 fs from survey data are the subagent's derivation (Medium), not stated values.
- **Stated jitter values in abstracts:** M. Straayer et al., *ISSCC* 2016, paper 27.5, DOI 10.1109/ISSCC.2016.7418108 ("SNR is dominated by aperture jitter of 50fs" at 3.8 GHz); S. Devarajan et al., *ISSCC* 2009, DOI 10.1109/ISSCC.2009.4977320 (65 fs); A. M. A. Ali et al., *ISSCC* 2010, DOI 10.1109/ISSCC.2010.5433923 (60 fs).

## R-368 · 3GPP NR handset receiver requirements and the sensitivity derivation (Course 21)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent: TS 38.101-1 V19.7.0 (2026-09) and TR 38.817-01 V16.4.0 (2022-09), DOCX from the 3GPP FTP archive.*

- **TS 38.101-1 V19.7.0** §7.3: REFSENS is "the minimum mean power applied to each one of the UE antenna ports ... at which the throughput shall meet or exceed the requirements for the specified reference measurement channel"; throughput "≥ 95 %"; QPSK. Table 7.3.2-1a (two antenna ports, FDD), n1 at 15 kHz SCS: −100.0 / −96.8 / −93.8 / −89.6 dBm for 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 MHz; NOTE 2 "The transmitter shall be set to PUMAX". Table 7.3.2-1b: n78 at 30 kHz "−96.1 + 10log10(NRB/24)" dBm. NOTE 8: "The REFSENS value is rounded to the nearest number down to one decimal point." 4Rx and 8Rx allowances (Tables 7.3.2-2, 7.3.2-2a) and the XR two-port allowance −1.0 dB (Table 7.3.2-2b). [Established]
- **Interference tests (same TS):** ACS (§7.5) 33 dB for 3–10 MHz below 2.7 GHz, interferers up to −25 dBm; in-band blocking (§7.6.2) −56 / −44 dBm; out-of-band CW blocking (§7.6.3) −44 / −30 / −15 dBm by range (−20 dBm above 6 GHz); narrow-band blocking (§7.6.4) −55 dBm CW; wide-band intermodulation (§7.8.2) "PInterferer 1 (CW)" −46 dBm and "PInterferer 2 (Modulated)" −46 dBm with FInterferer 2 = 2 × FInterferer 1, wanted at REFSENS + 6 to 9 dB; maximum input level (§7.4) −25 dBm. [Established]
- **TR 38.817-01 V16.4.0** §6.2: "Sensitivity = -174dBm(kT) + 10*log(RX BW) + NF + SNR +IM – diversity gain"; SNR "−1dB"; "the diversity gain is 3dB and the Implementation Margin (IM) uses 2.5dB"; "The NF for the NR bands can reuse those for E-UTRA. For the three new NR bands, i.e. Bands n77~79, the agreed NR values are 10.5dB, 10dB and 10dB respectively." The 9 dB for legacy bands is inferred by reconstructing the n1 values (−99.97 and −96.79 dBm before rounding); no direct statement was found (open issue). [Established for quoted text; Industry estimate for the inferred 9 dB]

## R-421 · Efficiency standards and USB Power Delivery (Course 22)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (curl through the session proxy; HTML and PDF text extracted). R-122 holds the 80 PLUS power-factor details; R-098 holds the earlier USB PD 3.1 excerpts, superseded here by the 3.3 text.*

- **CLEAResult, "80 PLUS: What do the different PSU ratings mean?"** [Established]:
  - 115 V internal non-redundant, at 5/10/20/50/100% load: Titanium – / 90 / 92 / 94 / 90%; Ruby 85 / 91 / 93 / 95 / 91%.
  - 230 V and 277 V internal redundant, at 10/20/50/100%: Platinum "88% | 90% | 94% PFC ≥ 0.95 | 91%" (with "230V - 10% efficiency criteria below Titanium are suggested"); Titanium "90% | 94% PFC ≥ 0.95 | 96% | 91%"; Ruby at 5/10/20/50/100% "90% … | 91% … | 95% … | 96.5% … | 92%".
  - 380 V DC, 800 V DC, 400 V and 480 V internal redundant: Ruby "91% | 95% | 97% | 92%".
- **US DOE, 88 FR 7284 (2 Feb 2023), Table II.1, restating 10 CFR 430.32(w)** (Level VI, for external power supplies manufactured on or after 10 Feb 2016) [Established]:
  - Single-voltage AC-DC, basic-voltage: "1 W < Pout <= 49 W … >= 0.071 x ln(Pout)-0.0014 x Pout + 0.67 … <= 0.100"; "49 W < Pout <= 250 W … >= 0.880 … <= 0.210"; "Pout > 250 W … >= 0.875 … <= 0.500". Efficiencies are decimals; the last figure is maximum no-load power in W.
  - The low-voltage block (< 6 V nameplate, ≥ 550 mA) uses 0.0834 ln(P) − 0.0014P + 0.609 for 1–49 W and 0.870 for 49–250 W (the notice mislabels this block "Basic-Voltage").
  - Tighter levels proposed in 2023 were not found adopted (unverified).
- **Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, Annex II and Art. 2, from 1 Apr 2020** (legislation.gov.uk "as adopted" copy; EUR-Lex blocked) [Established]:
  - "'average active efficiency' means the average of the active mode efficiencies at 25 %, 50 %, 75 % and 100 % of the nameplate output power".
  - The AC-DC formulas equal the US ones. No-load ≤ 0.10 W up to 49 W and ≤ 0.21 W above (AC-DC). The "Efficiency at low load (10 %)" must be declared, except for supplies of 10 W or less.
- **USB-IF, *USB Power Delivery Specification*, Revision 3.3, Version 1.0, 16 Oct 2026** (document library entry dated 11/05/2026) [Established]:
  - "Extends the power range from a maximum of 100W (SPR) to a maximum of 240W (EPR)".
  - "EPR PDO … Fixed Supply PDO that offers either 28V, 36V or 48V".
  - "up to 240W (48V/5A)".
- **Sources:** [80 PLUS ratings](https://www.clearesult.com/80plus/80plus-psu-ratings-explained); [88 FR 7284](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-02-02/html/2023-01282.htm); [EU 2019/1782 Annex II](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2019/1782/annex/II/adopted); [USB PD library](https://www.usb.org/document-library/usb-power-delivery). ## R-424 · Buck power-stage design references (Course 22)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by the main agent (curl through the session proxy, pdftotext); the DA9063 entry was read by a research subagent the same day.*

- **B. Hauke, *Basic Calculation of a Buck Converter's Power Stage*, Texas Instruments SLVA477C (Dec 2011, revised Sep 2026)** [Established, vendor application note]:
  - "A good estimation for the inductor ripple current is 20% to 40% of the output current".
  - $C_{OUT(min)} = \Delta I_L/(8 \times f_S \times \Delta V_{OUT})$ and "ΔVOUT(ESR) = ESR × ΔIL".
  - Ceramic dielectric "must be X5R or better. Otherwise, the capacitor loses much of its capacitance due to dc bias or temperature."
- **TI *LMR33630* data sheet, SNVSAN3F (Aug 2017, revised Nov 2020)** [Established as data-sheet values]:
  - "Short minimum on-time of 68 ns"; "Frequency: 400 kHz, 1.4 MHz, 2.1 MHz"; "Low operating quiescent current of 25 µA"; "Peak efficiency > 95%".
  - §8.4.3: "the LMR33630 automatically reduces the switching frequency when the minimum on-time limit is reached".
- **TI *TPS62840* data sheet, SLVSEC6D** [Established as data-sheet values]:
  - PFM "generates a single switching pulse to ramp up the inductor current and recharge the output capacitor, followed by a sleep period".
  - Its Equation 2 sets the on-time to $(V_{OUT}/V_{IN}) \times 556$ ns, and its Equation 3 gives the PFM frequency.
  - "The boundary between PWM and PFM mode is when the inductor current becomes discontinuous".
  - Forced PWM "reduces or eliminates interference with RF and noise-sensitive circuits, but reduces efficiency at light loads".
  - 100% mode: "VINmin = VOUT + IOUT × (RDS(on)max + RL)".
- **"High CV MLCC DC BIAS Capacitance Loss Explained," EEPower, 31 Jul 2019** [Industry estimate]: "The loss at rated voltage can vary from -35% to -65% at rated voltage" (10 µF 6.3 V X7R 0805, three vendors).
- **Renesas DA9063 product page** [Established]: "Six buck converters, 0.3 V to 3.34 V up to 2.5 A"; "Dual-phase mode up to 5 A"; "11 LDO regulators, 0.6 V to 3.6 V up to 300 mA"; feature list includes "Dynamic Voltage Scaling (DVS)"; "High efficiency is achieved over a wide load range by automatically selecting Pulse Frequency Modulation (PFM) or Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) modes."
- **Sources:** [SLVA477C](https://www.ti.com/lit/an/slva477b/slva477b.pdf) (the URL serves revision C); [LMR33630](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lmr33630.pdf); [TPS62840](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps62840.pdf); [EEPower](https://eepower.com/technical-articles/high-cv-mlcc-dc-bias-capacitance-loss-explained/); [DA9063](https://www.renesas.com/en/products/da9063). ## R-433 · Converter compensation and slope-compensation guidance (Course 22)

*Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (PDF text checked).*

- **TI TPS55288 data sheet, SLVSF01B (rev. Dec 2020), §8.2.2.7** [Established]: "It is generally accepted that the loop gain cross over 0 dB at the frequency no higher than the lower of either 1/10 of the switching frequency, fSW or 1/5 of the RHPZ frequency, fRHPZ"; "Designing the loop for greater than 45° of phase margin and greater than 10-dB gain margin eliminates output voltage ringing during the line and load transient."
- **Renesas (Intersil) TB417, Rev 1.00, Dec 2003** [Established, vendor rule of thumb]: "For synchronous and non-synchronous buck converters, the bandwidth should be between 20 to 30% of the switching frequency"; "The Type III network, however, utilizes two zeroes to give a phase boost of 180o"; "placing the zero at 50% of the output filter double pole frequency"; "placing the first pole at the ESR zero frequency"; "Set the second pole at half the switching frequency and also set the second zero at the output filter double pole."
- **TI SLVA662, July 2014** [Established]: "Phase margins of 45 degrees to 60 degrees … are considered safe values that yield well-damped transient load response"; "The Type III compensator is used when more than 90 degrees of phase boost are necessary."
- **TI LM25117 data sheet, SNVS714F (rev. Aug 2015), §8.3.2** [Established]: "Peak current mode regulators can exhibit unstable behavior when operating above 50% duty cycle. This behavior is known as sub-harmonic oscillation and is characterized by alternating wide and narrow pulses at the SW pin." (Its quoted Q of 0.673 at K = 1 conflicts with its own formula, which gives 2/π ≈ 0.637; not used.)
- **TI LM5155 data sheet, SNVSB75E (rev. Aug 2023), §9.3.6** [Established]: "the slope of the compensation ramp must be greater than half of the sensed inductor current falling slope to prevent subharmonic oscillation at high duty cycle"; "Typically 82% of the sensed inductor current falling slope is known as an optimal amount of the slope compensation."
- **Classic papers (Crossref-verified):** Middlebrook and Ćuk, IEEE PESC 1976, pp. 18–34, doi:10.1109/PESC.1976.7072895; Vorpérian, IEEE Trans. AES 26(3):490–496, 1990, doi:10.1109/7.106126; Ridley, IEEE Trans. Power Electronics 6(2):271–280, 1991, doi:10.1109/63.76813.
- **Sources:** [TPS55288](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55288.pdf); [TB417](https://www.renesas.com/us/en/document/oth/tb417-designing-stable-compensation-networks-single-phase-voltage-mode-buck-regulators); [SLVA662](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/slva662); [LM25117](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm25117.pdf); [LM5155](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm5155.pdf). Checked Nov 2026.

  - "auto-controlled Hysteretic mode for high efficiency down to 1 µA load currents"; auto mode switches to PWM at 90 mA and back at 40 mA; PWM at 3.6 MHz; ripple 5 mVpp (PWM) against 50 mVpp (hysteretic).
- **Sources:** [TPS65219](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps65219.pdf); [TPS6594-Q1](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps6594-q1.pdf); nPM1300 PS v1.3, read from a public copy at github.com (Liesegang/env_sensor, docs/datasheets) because Nordic's own site served a bot challenge. *Read on 24 Nov 2026 by a research subagent.*

- **P. Keil et al., "Calendar Aging of Lithium-Ion Batteries: I. Impact of the Graphite Anode on Capacity Fade," *J. Electrochem. Soc.* 163(9):A1872–A1880, 2016 (CC BY 4.0)** [Established]: NCA, NMC and LFP 18650 cells stored at 16 SoCs and 25/40/50 °C for about 9–10 months; "calendar aging does not increase steadily with the SoC. Instead, plateau regions, covering SoC intervals of more than 20%–30% of the cell capacity…"; "Lower anode potentials … promote solid electrolyte interphase growth … main driver of capacity fade during storage"; LFP "ca. 0.2 percentage points of capacity fade per month at 25◦ C and … ca. 0.5 percentage points per month at 50◦ C"; "For long-term storage, the graphite anode should be lithiated less than 50%."
- **Y. Preger et al., "Degradation of Commercial Lithium-Ion Cells as a Function of Chemistry and Cycling Conditions," *J. Electrochem. Soc.* 167:120532, 2020 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)** [Established]: LFP "2500 to 9000 EFC vs 250 to 1500 EFC for NCA cells and 200 to 2500 EFC for NMC cells" (to 80% capacity); "SOC range affects % capacity for the NCA and NMC cells similarly (5%–10% lower at 0%–100%), but SOC range has little effect on the capacity for LFP cells."
- **Battery University, BU-808 (updated 11 Oct 2023)** [Industry estimate; the table says "All values are estimated"]: "every reduction in peak charge voltage of 0.10V/cell is said to double the cycle life".
- **Battery University, BU-802b (updated 2 Nov 2021)** [Industry estimate]: "Li-ion self-discharges about 5 percent in the first 24 hours and then loses 1–2 percent per month; the protection circuit adds another 3 percent per month." Its Table 4 appears to repeat BU-808's one-year recoverable-capacity data as monthly self-discharge and is not used [Contested].

## R-454 · Inertia, RoCoF and inverter-based-resource disturbances (Course 22)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent.*

- **ENTSO-E, *Inertia and Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF)* v17 (16 Dec 2020)** [Established]: mean inertia constants nuclear 5.9 s, gas and hard coal 4.2 s, lignite 3.8 s, hydro 2.7–3.7 s, wind and solar 0; "transients with RoCoF higher than 1 Hz/s are not manageable by system protections".
- **ENTSO-E RoCoF withstand guidance (31 Jan 2018)** [Established]: ±2 Hz/s over 500 ms, ±1.5 Hz/s over 1000 ms, ±1.25 Hz/s over 2000 ms.
- **ERCOT inertia white paper (rev. 2 Dec 2024)** [Established]: critical inertia about 100 GW·s for a 2,805 MW loss; lowest recorded 109 GW·s on 22 Mar 2021; IBR inertia 0. The criterion (re-read during the course audit, 25 Nov 2026): after the 2,805 MW loss, frequency must take at least 0.416 s, the deployment time of ERCOT's load resources, to fall from 59.7 Hz to the 59.3 Hz first stage of under-frequency load shedding. The 1 Hz/s protection limit is ENTSO-E's, not ERCOT's.
- **NERC, *Odessa Disturbance* (Sep 2021)** [Established]: total loss 1,340 MW, of which solar PV 1,112 MW; the largest single cause PLL loss of synchronism (389 MW).
- **NERC, *2022 Odessa Disturbance* (Dec 2022)** [Established]: 844 MW synchronous plus 1,711 MW IBR, "a total loss of 2,555 MW"; the event "nearly exceeded" the Texas resource-loss protection criteria.
- **Sources:** [ENTSO-E inertia](https://eepublicdownloads.azureedge.net/clean-documents/SOC%20documents/Inertia%20and%20RoCoF_v17_clean.pdf); [ENTSO-E RoCoF](https://eepublicdownloads.entsoe.eu/clean-documents/Network%20codes%20documents/NC%20RfG/IGD_RoCoF_withstand_capability_final.pdf); [ERCOT](https://www.ercot.com/files/docs/2018/04/04/Inertia_Basic%20Concepts%20and%20Impacts%20on%20the%20ERCOT%20Grid_2024.docx); [NERC 2021](https://www.nerc.com/pa/rrm/ea/Documents/Odessa_Disturbance_Report.pdf); [NERC 2022](https://www.nerc.com/comm/RSTC_Reliability_Guidelines/NERC_2022_Odessa_Disturbance_Report%20(1).pdf). ## R-481 · Write-amplification models and flash error correction (Course 23)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by the main agent (papers opened).*

- **Desnoyers, SYSTOR 2012** [Established: peer-reviewed]: for LRU (FIFO) cleaning under uniform random writes, survival $S = (1 - 1/U)^{T/A}$ and $A = 1/(1 - S)$, converging as $U \to \infty$ to $A = \alpha/(\alpha + W(-\alpha e^{-\alpha}))$ with $\alpha = T/U$ (equations 1–4); greedy cleaning is optimal for uniform random traffic (citing Hu); Table 2, greedy, analytic $A$ at spare factor $S_f$: 0.03 → 13.624, 0.05 → 8.872, 0.07 → 6.623, 0.11 → 4.430, 0.17 → 3.002, matching simulation to about three decimals.
- **Cai, Ghose, Haratsch, Luo and Mutlu, *Proc. IEEE*, Sep 2017 (arXiv:1706.08642)** [Established: peer-reviewed survey]: read-retry is "widely implemented today" but can significantly increase read latency; the LDPC error-correction flow tries hard decoding, then multiple levels of soft decoding using soft information from multiple reads, then superpage-level parity; the example flow figure shows about 80 µs per hard-decoding iteration and per soft level, and about 10 ms for superpage-level parity recovery.
- **Sources:** [Desnoyers](https://www.ccs.neu.edu/home/pjd/papers/pjd-systor12.pdf); [Cai et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.08642). Checked Nov 2026. The Hu et al. SYSTOR 2009 PDF did not download and is cited only through Desnoyers.

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by the main agent (full text via the Europe PMC API; the PMC and Springer pages served browser checks and were not used).*

- **Hellenbrand, Teck and MacManus-Driscoll, "Progress of emerging non-volatile memory technologies in industry," *MRS Communications* 14, 1099–1112 (7 Nov 2024)** [Established: review of public company data]. Table 2, "Summary of top metrics": endurance FeRAM 10¹⁵ (Infineon, TI), PCRAM >10⁷ (IBM/Macronix, SK hynix), RRAM 10¹² (Samsung), STT-MRAM 10¹⁶ (Avalanche), NOR flash 10⁴–10⁶, DRAM and SRAM 10¹⁶; retention FeRAM 121 years at 85 °C (Infineon), PCRAM >10 years at 150 °C (ST), RRAM 10 years at 105 °C (TSMC), STT-MRAM 20 years at 150 °C (TSMC) and 10⁶ years at 65 °C (Renesas); write speed 2 ns, ≤20 ns, 5/1 ns set/reset, 1.5 ns, NOR 0.1–1 ms; read speed 2 ns, ≤30 ns, <5 ns, 4 ns; switching voltage 0.5 V, <3 V, <1–1.5 V, 0.8–2.0 V, NOR >5 V; cell write energy <100 fJ (projected), 2.63 pJ set and 1.5–9 pJ reset, 5 fJ, 0.7 pJ, NOR ~100 pJ, DRAM ~10 fJ; integration node NOR flash 28 nm. The review states that eNVM's main target is replacing embedded flash and that RRAM and MRAM are the most developed.

Alpha is a multiplier based on the user's selection of BER. For example, for BER = 10-12, alpha = 14.07." Also: "Dj(δδ) is not a 'peak-to-peak' or 'full scale' measure."
- **Derived here (scipy):** $Q^{-1}$ = 4.753, 5.998, 7.034 and 7.941 at 1e-6, 1e-9, 1e-12 and 1e-15, so $2Q^{-1}(10^{-12})$ = 14.07. Setting $\tfrac12Q(x)$ = 1e-12 gives 13.87, and Keysight's $\rho_T$ = 1 form (R-063) gives 14.26. The 24-02 lab fits a dual-Dirac line to 3 ps peak-to-peak sinusoidal jitter plus 0.4 ps rms random jitter and gets DJ(δδ) = 2.44 ps (1e-9/1e-12 fit), illustrating the quote.
- **Sources:** [Teledyne LeCroy](https://teledynelecroy.com/doc/docview.aspx?id=8423); see also R-063 (Keysight 5989-3206EN). Checked Nov 2026.

## R-507 · IEEE 802.3dj error-ratio allocations, jitter corner and COM reference receivers (Course 24)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (documents opened; COM workbooks downloaded and cells read).*

- **802.3dj Key Motions (16 May 2024)** [Established for the task-force motions; final clause values not read]: "Move to adopt DER_0 = 2e−4 for 200 Gb/s per lane backplane and copper cable PMD link" (Nov 2023); all AUIs within a PHY combined at "DER0 value of 2.67e-5 (equivalent to measured BER of 4e-5 with precoding ON)"; "Move to adopt C2C DER_0 = 0.67E-5 and C2M DER_0 = 2E-5" (Sep 2023); a jitter-tolerance and clock-recovery corner of 4 MHz ("fBaud/26562.5") for RS544-based PMDs and AUIs. *Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (document opened).*

Riani (Inphi), "FEC Latency and Power/Area Tradeoffs for 100G KR/CR," IEEE P802.3ck, Sep 2019** [Industry estimate: one company's implementation numbers]: Clause 91 RS(544,514) "Block Time 51 ns", "Processing 100 ns", "Total 151"; an interleaved RS(544,514) 102 + 100 + 10 = 212 ns, "=> 61 ns increase in latency for interleaved FEC". ## R-513 · Concatenated FEC for 200 Gb/s optical lanes and 1.6 TbE FEC structure (Course 24)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (documents opened).*

- **L. Patra (Marvell), "Updates on Concatenated FEC Proposal for 200G/Lane PMD," IEEE 802.3df, 12 Jul 2022** [Industry estimate; the slide does not state its NCG convention]: RS(544,514) KP4 at 106.25 G, pre-FEC threshold 2.2E-4, NCG 7 dB; RS(576,514) at 112.5 G, 1.1E-3, 8 dB; RS(544,514) + Hamming(128,120) soft decision at 113.3 G, 4.85E-3, 9.5 dB; "Delta improvement over KP FEC=2.5dB"; soft-decision FEC "~100mW per 200G Lane" (N5).
- **L. Patra, A. Farhood, R. Radhamohan et al., "FEC baseline proposal for 200Gb/s per Lane IM-DD Optical PMDs," IEEE 802.3dj, Mar 2023** (adopted as motion 03-2023 #5, 70/5/15) [Established for the adopted baseline]: RS(544,514) outer code plus a Hamming-based (128,120) soft-decision inner code with a convolutional interleaver, for 200GBASE-DR1/FR1, 400GBASE-DR2 and 800GBASE-DR4/DR4-2/FR4; the inner code "Appends 8b parity to 120b payload" over 12 KP4 symbols from distinct RS codewords, with an 8-way Hamming interleave; "113.3333GBaud" without and "113.4375GBaud" with padding, "an integer multiple of 156.25M*726"; 384 pad bits per 3,264 Hamming codewords in the baseline (changed in Sep 2023 to 1,024-bit pads every 8,704 codewords); decoder-input BER threshold 4.85E-3 (AWGN); convolutional interleaver plus inner code latency "~140ns" (2-way) or "~56ns" (4-way). The same inner FEC was adopted for 1.6TbE SMF PMDs (Jul 2023 #9); 200 G/lane copper and backplane use RS(544,514) only (May 2023 #6).
- **M. Gustlin et al., "1.6TbE PCS/FEC Baseline Proposal," Feb 2023** (adopted May 2023) [Established]: "RS(544,514) based FEC", "Keeps 4 FEC engines/codewords for excellent burst error tolerance"; 200 GbE and 400 GbE on 200 G/lanes use "4x RS codewords interleaving" (Jul 2023 #10).
- **Derived here (BPSK convention, NCG = 20 log10(Q_out/Q_in) + 10 log10 R):** KP4 at 2.2e-4: 6.16 dB (output 1e-13), 6.83 dB (1e-15); concatenated at 4.85e-3 with R = (514/544)(120/128): 8.54 and 9.22 dB; difference 2.38 dB. The slide's 7 and 9.5 dB are a few tenths above, consistent with a different convention.
- **Sources:** [Patra 2022](https://grouper.ieee.org/groups/802/3/df/public/22_07/patra_3df_01a_2207.pdf); [Patra et al. 2023](https://www.ieee802.org/3/dj/public/23_03/patra_3dj_01b_2303.pdf); [Gustlin et al. 2023](https://www.ieee802.org/3/dj/public/23_01/23_0206/gustlin_3dj_01b_230206.pdf); [802.3dj Key Motions](https://www.ieee802.org/3/dj/projdoc/KeyMotions_3dj_240516.pdf). *Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (consortium slides, a republished release, trade press and a Nature Electronics paper opened).*

Das Sharma, SNIA SDC 2024; IEEE HIR 2023 plenary) [Established as targets]: UCIe-S/UCIe-A/UCIe-3D: rates 4–32 GT/s (3D up to 4); widths 16/64/80; bump pitch 100–130 / 25–55 / under 10 µm optimized; reach under 25 mm / under 2 mm / vertical; shoreline "28 – 224 165 – 1317" GB/s/mm; areal 22–125 / 188–1,350 GB/s/mm², 4 TB/s/mm² at 9 µm for 3D; "Power Efficiency Target (pJ/b) 0.5 0.25 <0.05 at 9µm"; "Latency (Tx + Rx) < 2ns Includes D2D Adapter and PHY"; shoreline "Conservatively estimated: AP: 45u; Standard: 110u".
- **Nature Electronics** (D. Das Sharma, G. Pasdast, S. Tiagaraj, K. Aygün, 19 Feb 2024, doi:10.1038/s41928-024-01126-y) [Established, modelled]: "At 9 µm, the total power of the D2D link due to simplified architecture at 4 GT s−1 is 0.03 pJ b−1. At 1 µm, the total power drops to 0.015 pJ b−1"; forwarded-clock operation at 1 GT/s about 0.01 pJ/b; "the most power-efficient performance … can be achieved by reducing the frequency as the bump pitch goes down"; context: the external UCIe D2D power "0.25 pJ b−1 at 0.5 V running at 16 GT s−1".

## R-526 · Single-mode (G.652.D) and multimode (OM3–OM5) fiber specifications (Course 24)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (Prysmian datasheet PDF, a Fluke Networks knowledge article and the Fiber Optic Association's nomenclature page opened; the Corning SMF-28 Ultra datasheet returned "Access Denied" and was not used).* [Established]

- Prysmian's G.652.D-compliant single-mode fiber: maximum cabled attenuation ≤ 0.36 dB/km at 1310 nm and ≤ 0.22 dB/km at 1550 nm; chromatic dispersion ≤ 3.5 ps/(nm·km) over 1285–1330 nm, ≤ 18 at 1550 nm and ≤ 22 at 1625 nm; zero-dispersion wavelength 1300–1324 nm; mode-field diameter 9.2 ± 0.4 µm at 1310 nm; group index 1.467 at 1310 nm and 1.468 at 1550 nm. Quotes: "Maximum attenuation value of cable at 1310 nm … ≤ 0.36"; "At 1550 nm ps/km ● nm ≤ 18".
- TIA multimode values (via Fluke): cabled attenuation 3.0 dB/km at 850 nm for OM3/OM4/OM5 (3.5 for OM1/OM2), 1.5 dB/km at 1300 nm; minimum effective modal bandwidth at 850 nm 2,000 MHz·km (OM3) and 4,700 MHz·km (OM4/OM5). Quote: "OM3 50 µm 1500 500 2,000 OM4 50 µm 3500 500 4,700". FOA lists OM4 as "3600/500 MHz-km", a different (overfilled-launch) figure; the chapter uses the TIA EMB.
- The ITU-T G.652 table itself was not opened; the commonly quoted ITU cable maxima are not used.
- **Derived here:** fiber group delay $n_g/c$ = 1.468/c = 4.90 µs/km; 100 m of OM4 loses 0.3 dB at 850 nm.
- **Sources:** [Prysmian G.652.D datasheet](https://ec.prysmian.com/sites/ec.prysmian.com/files/media/documents/G652D.pdf); [Fluke Networks KA-05286](https://my.fluke.com/en-US/article/KA-05286); [FOA fiber nomenclature](https://thefoa.org/tech/OM.html). Checked Nov 2026.

## R-537 · TSMC COUPE silicon-photonics roadmap (Course 24)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (Tom's Hardware report of 3 Aug 2026 opened; TSMC's own newsroom served a bot challenge and was not used).* [Industry estimate: foundry roadmap as reported; multipliers are TSMC's claims]

- COUPE (Compact Universal Photonic Engine) "bonds a 65nm electronic integrated circuit (EIC) with a photonic integrated circuit (PIC) using the company's SoIC-X bonding technology". Three stages: COUPE on PCB (1.6T OSFP pluggables); COUPE on substrate, co-packaged with switch ASICs, up to 6.4 Tb/s per engine with "2x power efficiency, and 10x lower latency" than pluggables; COUPE on interposer, a 12.8 Tb/s engine with "5x power efficiency and 20x lower latency", described as exploratory with no date.
- Micro-ring roadmap: "The company plans to bring the world's first 200 Gbps/lane (wavelength) micro-ring modulator into production in 2026" at 0.5 Tb/s/mm, then 1 Tb/s/mm (2028), 2 Tb/s/mm (2029) and 4 Tb/s/mm with 400 Gb/s rings (2030).
- **Source:** [Tom's Hardware, CPO foundry roadmaps, 3 Aug 2026](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/co-packaged-optics-cpo-foundry-roadmaps-breaking-down-tsmc-intel-samsung-and-globalfoundries-approach-to-next-generation-scale-up-connectivity). Checked Nov 2026.

## R-543 · NVIDIA Spectrum-X and Quantum-X Photonics claims, 2025–2026 (Course 24)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (NVIDIA newsroom release, technical blog and product page opened).* [Industry estimate: vendor claims with vendor-chosen baselines]

- 18 Mar 2025 (GTC): "integrate optics innovations with 4x fewer lasers to deliver 3.5x more power efficiency", "63x greater signal integrity", "10x better network resiliency"; Spectrum-X Photonics at 100 and 400 Tb/s; Quantum-X Photonics 144 × 800G InfiniBand on 200G SerDes.

## R-546 · CPO reliability at Meta, and a datacenter-scale power scenario (Course 24)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (Broadcom release via Nasdaq and The Next Platform opened; Meta's ECOC 2025 paper itself was not obtained).* [Contested: vendor-announced or relayed; lab against field]

- Broadcom (1 Oct 2025): "Testing of Broadcom CPO solutions at Meta has demonstrated one million link hours without a single link flap", in a high-temperature lab environment; "CPO reduces optics power by 65 percent" against pluggables.
- The Next Platform, relaying Meta's paper: "each unit ran continuously without interruption or clearing the FEC [forward error correction] counters and we did not see any failures or uncorrectable codewords (UCWs) in the links"; pluggable failure rates came from field data and CPO's from lab stress; CPO used 35% less power per 100G lane than LPO; Meta presented no LPO reliability data.
- The same article relays a scenario: 6.4 million pluggables at 30 W (192 MW), or 64 MW with LPO at 10 W, against a CPO figure of 42 MW, 10.5% of 400 MW of accelerator power.
- Later figures of about 15 million and over 50 million CPO device-hours, and blast-radius warnings, were seen only in search excerpts and are **unconfirmed**.
- **Derived here:** 10⁶ device-hours = 114 device-years; with zero failures the 95% upper bound is −ln(0.05)/10⁶ h ≈ 3,000 FIT.
- **Sources:** [Broadcom CPO reliability (Nasdaq)](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/broadcom-showcases-industry-leading-quality-and-reliability-co-packaged-optics-2025); The Next Platform as in R-545. Checked Nov 2026.

- **Sources:** [ASML NXE:3800E](https://www.asml.com/en/products/euv-lithography-systems/twinscan-nxe-3800e); [ASML Annual Report 2025, strategic section](https://ourbrand.asml.com/m/8ab959d4926657b/original/asml-2025-annual-report-strategic-report-section.pdf). Checked Nov 2026.

## R-561 · ASML EXE:5000 and EXE:5200B (High-NA EUV) specifications (Course 25)

*Read on 25 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (ASML product pages and annual report opened).* [Established: vendor specification]

- EXE:5000: "Its 8 nm resolution will enable chipmakers to print with a single exposure features 1.7 times smaller – and therefore achieve transistor densities 2.9 times higher – than those possible using TWINSCAN NXE systems"; "The anamorphic mirrors require an exposure field half the size of that in NXE systems".
- Specifications: 0.55 NA; "Wafers per hour ≥ 110, At dose: 50 mJ/cm²" (EXE:5000) and "≥ 175, At dose: 50 mJ/cm²" (EXE:5200B).
- Annual report: "In early April 2025, we shipped our first TWINSCAN EXE:5200B system… At 175 wafers per hour, it offers 60% higher productivity compared to the TWINSCAN EXE:5000".
- **Derived here:** $k_1$ = 8 × 0.55/13.5 = 0.326; half field 26 × 16.5 mm = 429 mm².
- **Sources:** [EXE:5000](https://www.asml.com/en/products/euv-lithography-systems/twinscan-exe-5000); [EXE:5200B](https://www.asml.com/en/products/euv-lithography-systems/twinscan-exe-5200b); annual report as in R-560. Checked Nov 2026.

## R-562 · ASML NXT:2150i (ArF immersion), EUV replacing multipatterning, sole EUV supplier (Course 25)

- "Ajinomoto's film capacity was already running at full load in the second quarter of 2026, at a reported two million square meters per month"; "Ajinomoto notified substrate manufacturers in May 2026 that it would raise ABF film prices by approximately 30%, effective in the third quarter."
- An AI substrate example uses "about 3.5 times the board area and three times as many ABF layers as a conventional design — 18 layers against six — consuming roughly ten times as much ABF overall."
- Ibiden's roadmap: 90 × 90 mm substrates (2026), 110 × 110 mm (2028), 130 × 130 mm and larger later; organic substrates are reported to lose usable flatness beyond about 120 mm per side.

- **Derived here:** 3.5 × 18/6 = 10.5, consistent with "roughly ten times".
- **Source:** [Tom's Hardware, 10 Sep 2026](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/the-state-of-abf-substrates-in-data-center-silicon-in-2026-solving-the-supply-crunch-and-material-wall-beneath-every-ai-accelerator). Checked Nov 2026.

## R-593 · Hybrid-bonding research pitches and overlay (Course 25)

*Read on 26 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (imec, EVG, CEA-Leti and Bits&Chips pages opened).* [Established as research demonstrations, not production pitches]

- imec (19 Feb 2024): hybrid Cu/SiCN bonding "with interconnect pitches down to an unprecedented 400nm", reported at IEDM 2023; "for these 400nm interconnect pitches, overlay control needs to be smaller than 100nm".
- imec and EV Group (28 May 2026, ECTC 2026): 200 nm wafer-to-wafer pitch; "a Cu pad-to-pad post-bond overlay vector below 40nm was obtained for 100% of the dies over the full 300mm wafer".
- imec (29 May 2024): die-to-wafer "Cu bond pad pitch of only 2µm at <350nm die-to-wafer overlay error, achieving good electrical yield."
- CEA-Leti (29 May 2026): die-to-wafer "with pitches down to 1 μm"; "While the yield at 1 μm is limited by the alignment accuracy of existing bonding tools, the team anticipates significant improvements with the introduction of next-generation tools featuring 0.5 μm (3σ) alignment capabilities."
- Bits&Chips (28 May 2026): "In general, the required overlay accuracy of the bonding process corresponds to one-fourth of the pitch."
- **Derived here:** 200/4 = 50 nm against < 40 nm reported; 400/4 = 100 nm, matching imec's statement. "World first" and "record" are the labs' own words.
- **Sources:** [imec, 19 Feb 2024](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/wafer-wafer-hybrid-bonding-pushing-boundaries-400nm-interconnect-pitch); [imec, 28 May 2026](https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/imec-and-ev-group-demonstrate-wafer-wafer-hybrid-bonding-200nm-interconnect-pitch-and-record); [imec, 29 May 2024](https://imec-int.com/en/press/imec-demonstrates-die-wafer-hybrid-bonding-cu-interconnect-pad-pitch-2mm); [CEA-Leti, 29 May 2026](https://www.cea.fr/cea-tech/leti/english/Pages/What's-On/Press%20release/Die-to-Wafer-Hybrid-Bonding-Press-Release.aspx); [Bits&Chips, 28 May 2026](https://bits-chips.com/article/imec-and-evg-push-hybrid-bonding-to-200-nanometers/). ## R-605 · Black's equation, current exponents and copper transport paths (Course 25)

*Read on 26 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (three TU Wien theses opened).* [Established]

- Rovitto (TU Wien), §1.4.3: "a current density exponent n value close to 2 indicates a lognormal lifetime distribution, which corresponds to a nucleation time dominated failure …, while a value close to 1 indicates that the dominant phase of the electromigration failure time is the void evolution"; "Black's original empirical work predicted a failure time following a j-2 dependence, while later experimental studies estimated values of n generally lying between 1 and 3"; the two-phase form "MTTF = t_N + t_E = Bj^{-2} + Cj^{-1}".
- Orio (TU Wien), §1.3.1: "An exponent close to 1 indicates that the lifetime is dominated by the void growth mechanisms".
- Wessner (TU Wien), §5.1: "the activation energy and the current density exponent have to be determined experimentally and therefore its validity is limited to specific test configurations"; "In Cu interconnects, grain boundary and interface diffusion are the dominating transport mechanisms at normal temperature operating conditions".
- **Derived here:** for the two-phase form the local exponent is (2 + x)/(1 + x) with x = jC/B, tending to 2 at low j and 1 at high j. A quoted claim that n rises with current density was not found and is not used.
- **Sources:** [Rovitto, §1.4.3](https://www.iue.tuwien.ac.at/phd/rovitto/node24.html); [Orio, §1.3.1](https://www.iue.tuwien.ac.at/phd/orio/node16.html); [Wessner, §5.1](https://www.iue.tuwien.ac.at/phd/wessner/node25.html). Checked Nov 2026.

## R-610 · FIT definition and TI's HTOL example (Course 25)

*Read on 26 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (TI terminology and calculator pages and app note SNAA391 opened).* [Established]

- TI: "FIT – Failures in Time, number of units failing per billion operating hours."
- TI SNAA391 (Jun 2023): JEDEC JESD85 methods, of which "Most of these methods only apply to constant failure rates"; HTOL "sample size for HTOL is 7859, test duration is 1000 hours, the number of failures is zero, and the test temperature is 125 °C"; acceleration factor "78.6" (0.7 eV, 55 °C use); "the FIT value is calculated to be 1.5 for 55 °C operation"; "the confidence level is 60% (which is typical for industrial calculations)".

- **Derived here:** TI's 78.6 reproduces with k = 8.6 × 10⁻⁵ eV/K and T = °C + 273; exact constants give 77.6. χ²(0.60, 2) = 1.833; 1.833 × 10⁹/(2 × 1000 × 7859 × 78.6) = 1.48 FIT. A different 231-unit example reported elsewhere was not found in TI's pages and is not used.
- **Sources:** [TI reliability terminology](https://www.ti.com/quality-reliability/reliability/terminology.html); [TI reliability calculators](https://ti.com/support-quality/reliability/fail-fraction-average-fail-rate-fit.html); [TI SNAA391](https://www.ti.com/lit/an/snaa391/snaa391.pdf). *Read on 26 Nov 2026 by a research subagent (Wing VC and two SemiEngineering articles opened).* [Established for the historical 2%; Industry estimate and Contested for the rest]

- SemiEngineering (10 Mar 2020): "For decades, test was limited to a flat 2% of total manufacturing cost". SemiEngineering (11 May 2021): "For decades, test was limited to a flat 2% of the cost of designing and manufacturing a chip … the real cost of test now needs to be computed based on volume, complexity, and the cost of a failure."
